claims.title: Message packing, fields and signing match stored executed-reference vectors
claims.boundary: Named vector corpus; not live delivery.

claims.title: Direct and opportunistic delivery exchange messages with Python
claims.boundary: Pinned peer and the sizes/methods selected by each case.

claims.title: Propagation retrieval and peer synchronization exchange stored messages
claims.boundary: Peer authorization and non-default transfer limits remain test-specific.

claims.title: Impaired mixed transport paths retain delivery and cancellation behavior
claims.boundary: Named Python/.NET transport topologies, not RF.

claims.title: Ticket and ratchet persistence works across reference handoffs
claims.boundary: Selected reply-ticket and ratchet rotation/restart scenarios.

claims.title: Local router lifecycle, cancellation and rejection continue service
claims.boundary: Managed integration tests; not Python interoperability.

claims.title: Daemon rejects invalid arguments and configuration before opening a node
claims.boundary: Managed argument boundary plus optional published configuration rejection; neither alone proves daemon interoperability.

claims.title: Published daemon receives Python delivery and preserves its inbox over restart
claims.boundary: One-way daemon receipt; not bidirectional propagation.

claims.title: Published propagation daemon supports retrieval, control and autonomous peer recovery
claims.boundary: Six-case suite's explicit policy, timing and peer settings; no exhaustive failure matrix.

claims.title: Frames and signalling match the executed-reference corpus
claims.boundary: Stored vectors and malformed input; not live audio.

claims.title: Installed native codecs match reference bitstreams
claims.boundary: Installed Opus/Codec2 versions and profile corpus; not audio hardware.

claims.title: Stream packets, codecs and signals exchange over mixed paths
claims.boundary: Named direct/Python/.NET transport topologies only.

claims.title: Python telephone setup, profiles, teardown and rejection recover
claims.boundary: Virtual audio; no physical quality claim.

claims.title: Managed audio processing and device ownership preserve local contracts
claims.boundary: Fakes and executed vectors, not physical devices.

claims.title: Published phone validates CLI and persists configuration/identity
claims.boundary: Platform-specific CLI/process cases.

claims.title: Two published native phones exchange codec frames and recover
claims.boundary: Windows synthetic silence or Linux virtual audio; no Python peer claim.

claims.title: Published phone originates and answers actual Python calls
claims.boundary: Linux virtual audio, not physical hardware.

claims.title: Native telemetry format rejects unknown versions and publishes directly and through a transport hop
claims.boundary: A .NET-only format, no upstream compatibility target.

claims.title: Native address, Micron subset and state-store contracts remain bounded
claims.boundary: Initial textual subset; not full Micron/Urwid parity.

claims.title: Published terminal client retains identity and local state
claims.boundary: Native CLI/process behavior, no reference peer.

claims.title: Actual upstream node serves pages/files and exchanges messages with native client
claims.boundary: Linux direct/Python-hop/native-hop selections are separate runs; no impaired-network or full application-parity claim. Declared upstream dependency minimums exceed tested pins.

claims.title: Original desktop navigation, preferences, validation and shutdown preserve application state
claims.boundary: Original Avalonia UI subset, not pixel or feature parity.

claims.title: Application core exchanges direct text messages with pinned Python LXMF
claims.boundary: LXMF peer, not the complete upstream Sideband GUI or shared-instance coexistence.

claims.title: Published native application preserves identity and renders validation feedback
claims.boundary: Actual window/renderer on selected display; no hardware audio.

claims.title: Actual reference imports reject source drift and incorrect checkouts
claims.boundary: Module/revision/hash verification, not publisher authentication or a fresh network fetch.

claims.title: Automatic map discovery and arbitrary Python plugins
claims.boundary: Not implemented; reported interface/connection overlays, bounded raster maps, manual telemetry and public HTTPS mirroring have separate scoped claims, not automatic discovery, full application parity or Python-plugin ABI support.

claims.title: Physical RF mesh and physical audio interoperability
claims.boundary: One read-only identified board and synthetic audio do not establish this.

claims.title: Upstream-shaped JSON settings import/export applies supported keys and preserves unsupported keys
claims.boundary: Executed export statements and native settings exchange; not upstream SQLite, identity or binary config migration.

claims.title: Automatic/manual propagation selection and inbox retrieval recover across application restart
claims.boundary: Actual Python announcement/client and Python transport/propagation node; reference ignores the inactive flag. No impaired-network application claim.

claims.title: Disconnect/disposal cancels pending lookup and drains bounded conversation persistence
claims.boundary: Managed application lifecycle and isolated observers; no prolonged-operation soak claim.

claims.title: Bounded file attachments exchange with Python LXMF and remain exportable after restart
claims.boundary: Two-way 2 MiB direct LXMF fields; not audio/image handling, an upstream Sideband app peer or published-native file flow.

claims.title: Periodic propagation inbox checks preserve strict timing and retry state across restart
claims.boundary: Executed policy vectors and a real two-minute managed-app/Python-node run; not an hours-long soak or published-native scheduled-transfer flow. Native intervals are positive whole seconds.

claims.title: Failed delivery can retry once through propagation without duplicating local history
claims.boundary: Actual Python link refusal, propagation retrieval and direct-service recovery with policy enabled/disabled; not arbitrary packet-loss impairment.

claims.title: Actual primary application core exchanges direct and propagated messages in both directions
claims.boundary: Unmodified daemon core, direct TCP and Python transport/propagation node; database API observations, not the upstream GUI or physical hardware.

claims.title: Offline desktop identity, binary settings and SQLite WAL history import atomically
claims.boundary: Absent destination only; bounded conversation/trust/unread/text/file/image/audio/method activation. Known router, synchronization and supported telemetry activate separately. Voice and unsupported properties remain archive-only; transport interfaces are not migrated.

claims.title: Conversation trust, unread state and reply tickets survive application restart
claims.boundary: Executed policy/persistence methods, original foreground desktop controls and actual daemon-core direct/propagated ticket exchange with trust on/off; no voice authorization or telemetry-access claim.

claims.title: Bounded image and audio messages compose, persist, export and interoperate with actual Sideband
claims.boundary: Actual daemon-core direct/Python-transport-propagation cases, independently executed media vectors, fake-device UI and published offline decoding/rendering. Skia/Pillow image bytes differ; native Ogg fixes the reference helper's quarter-duration granule defect. No physical capture/acoustic or voice-call claim.

claims.title: Known client-router tickets ratchets stamp costs and duplicate caches migrate atomically
claims.boundary: Five bounded known client files, own signed ratchets and actual Python reverse cross-load; excludes propagation-node stores, foreign ratchets, unknown files and interfaces.

claims.title: Upstream SQLite synchronization anchors and retry state activate after offline migration
claims.boundary: Actual upstream database/WAL and policy observations; only lxmf.lastsync and lxmf.syncretrying activate, unknown properties remain archived. Request admission is not transfer completion.

claims.title: Voice policy, device ownership, original ringtone and persisted call state follow observed application contracts
claims.boundary: Executed policy/timing/callback vectors, fake devices and native-node lifecycle; original sound is not the licensed upstream ringtone. No physical capture/acoustics or upstream database call-log migration.

claims.title: Actual primary application core exchanges Opus Codec2 and PTT calls with the native application
claims.boundary: Both origins, direct and .NET transport; separate coordinator and shared-client trust/history/restart cases. Linux virtual Pulse; Windows explicitly replaces reference audio device factories with synthetic/discard backends. No Python transport, impairment or physical-audio claim for these Sideband-specific cases.

claims.title: Published native application pairs exchange codec frames and retain call history after restart
claims.boundary: Both origins, Opus-to-Codec2 progress, mute and restart using explicit synthetic/discard devices; not a Python peer or real microphone/speaker.

claims.title: Native daemon and bounded interactive voice extension support cancellation and closed stdin
claims.boundary: Actual primary voice handlers are placeholders; functional native commands extend them. EOF exits interactive mode but not the daemon. Native verbose/interactive/synthetic switches require daemon mode.

claims.title: Bounded raster cache offline MBTiles and original map viewport follow observed reference geometry
claims.boundary: Executed vectors, real loopback HTTP, immutable SQLite snapshots and original native rendering. Explicit online consent and bounded quotas differ intentionally. No public-provider, physical-location, upstream GUI, clustering or connection/interface overlay claim.

claims.title: Manual telemetry controls persist privacy tracking and report inspection with explicit provenance
claims.boundary: Original headless UI and published manual preview, no hardware or network collection. Admission is not delivery; collector inner source is not authenticated origin. Live telemetry transport requires separate evidence.

claims.title: Frozen native pair sustains an actual one-hour call and recovers from peer loss
claims.boundary: Explicit opt-in and expected binary hash, direct loopback synthetic/discard devices, sampled bounded memory/progress and Opus-to-Codec2 switch. No physical audio, Python-peer, multi-hop endurance or days-long service claim.

claims.title: Explicit public HTTPS mirror serves bounded static files with private certificate lifecycle
claims.boundary: Executed handler/certificate observations, real loopback TLS and original desktop/native flows. Default loopback, explicit consent, bounded GET-only jail and persistent certificate deliberately differ. No copied assets, automatic downloads, physical LAN/firewall, public trust-store, primary GUI or arbitrary Python-plugin claim.

claims.title: Manual telemetry reports collector requests streams privacy and supported persistence interoperate
claims.boundary: Executed policy/enrichment/schedule vectors and actual daemon-core direct/Python-hop reports, restart, SQLite/profile import and disclosed propagation fault injection. Native signature/cursor/retention safeguards and persisted slot counters deliberately differ. No automatic/physical sensors, upstream GUI, .NET-hop telemetry, arbitrary impairment, published-native network telemetry or prolonged-service claim.

claims.title: Bounded software paper QR encoding and pixel decoding preserve upstream defaults
claims.boundary: Actual upstream QR pixels and independent zxing-cpp decoding of Windows/Linux native PNGs. Envelope validation is not authentication; no physical camera, printer or macOS claim.

claims.title: Paper creation ingestion history URI and QR export survive application restart
claims.boundary: Actual primary daemon cores both ways, trust on/off and real process restarts; bounded native admission; separate published offline exports and original rendered desktop controls. No automatic forwarding, hardware scanning, upstream GUI or complete paper-history migration.

claims.title: Mutable delivery display names update announcements and solicited path responses
claims.boundary: Executed provider vectors plus native two-node announcements/path responses; no implicit persistence or announcement.

claims.title: Map presets and supported offline profile view activation preserve observed provider and layer contracts
claims.boundary: Executed provider/layer/clamp observations, original desktop controls, atomic profile activation and selected native persistence. Own API keys, HTTPS and explicit consent deliberately differ; no public-provider, complete migration, upstream GUI or physical-location claim.

claims.title: Authorized built-in remote commands and unknown-conversation admission preserve observed application policy
claims.source: sbapp/sideband/core.py command and delivery methods; docs/sideband.md
claims.boundary: Executed primary parsing/admission observations, actual daemon cores and bounded native queue/history/restart, original desktop and published command/reply/cancellation flows. Native signature, UTF-8 and resource bounds deliberately differ. Legacy native contact origins cannot be reconstructed; old contacts remain known. No arbitrary Python-plugin ABI, remote shell, complete command-service parity or physical-signal measurement claim.

claims.title: Reported map overlays object classification and local fixed locations preserve executed primary contracts
claims.source: sbapp/ui/map.py; sbapp/sideband/core.py object and fixed-location methods; docs/sideband.md
claims.boundary: Executed primary clustering/scatter/interface/connection, SQLite classification and file-loader observations; original bounded desktop filters, persistence, object workflows and explicit atomic overrides; separate native synthetic-profile rendering. Zero coordinates and atomic rejection of malformed/nonfinite overrides intentionally differ. Reported connection points are not edges or authenticated locations. No automatic discovery, physical sensors, primary GUI or new live-network overlay claim.
